question: If an item is bought for ₹800 and sold for ₹740, what is the loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of CP : SP = 800 : 740 = 40 : 37

Loss in ratio = 40 − 37 = 3 parts

Loss % = (3 ÷ 40) × 100 = 7.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 CP = ₹800
 
 
 SP = ₹740
 
 
• 
 
 
 
 

 
 

 Loss = ₹60
 Loss % = 7.5%

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹800

Selling Price (SP) = ₹740

**Formula Used:**

Loss = CP − SP

Loss Percentage = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Loss = 800 − 740 = ₹60

⇒ Loss Percentage = (60 ÷ 800) × 100

⇒ Loss Percentage = 6000 ÷ 800

⇒ Loss Percentage = 60 ÷ 8 = 7.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage

Profit occurs when SP > CP. Formula: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discount

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the equivalent single discount is (x + y − x × y ÷ 100)%.
